estoque-ci4.title: ERP Aplication for small business (CodeIgniter 4)
estoque-ci4.oneLiner: Simplified initial application for management of small business
estoque-ci4.problem: An optician's shop was performing operations manually using spreadsheets, which could directly impact its long-term performance.
solution: Creation of complete CRUD within essential modules (service orders, clients, users)
Application entirely created and exported using a MySQL relational database
Pursuit of clean-code methodology, in order to facilitate development
estoque-ci4.context: Operational system for an optical store that needed to centralize service orders, customers, inventory, payments, and indicators in a single workflow. The goal was to reduce spreadsheet dependency and make service, cash flow, and management more predictable.
responsibilities: Modeled and implemented modules for orders, customers, inventory, users, payments, and reports.
Structured role-based access rules for seller, manager, and administrator actions.
Implemented total recalculation, open balance, and validations to avoid financial inconsistencies.
Connected inventory and orders through async autocomplete search with pagination.
Added web session authentication and a foundation for JWT authentication in API endpoints.
technicalDecisions: Used CodeIgniter 4 with Models, Controllers, Filters, and Views to keep a clear MVC structure.
Applied soft delete to important entities to avoid permanent loss of operational records.
Normalized money and date inputs before persistence to handle Brazilian input formats.
Recalculated order totals from items instead of trusting manually editable values.
Used route filters to protect sensitive features by minimum permission level.
learnings: Simple business rules in the UI can require careful backend handling to avoid incorrect balances, totals, or payments.
Internal systems need predictability: validation, feedback, and permissions matter as much as making the screen work.
Connecting inventory, orders, and payments requires stable data contracts and attention to legacy cases.
Useful dashboards depend more on consistent queries and periods than only on visual presentation.
nextSteps: Add more tests for financial rules and permissions.
Improve auditing for changes in orders, payments, and inventory.
Improve setup documentation, migrations, and seeders.
Expand API endpoints with clear scopes for future integrations.
